options.label: keep the split
options.consequence: eleven careful, eight quick, as now: the ones judging truth and derivation read carefully, the ones judging shape and uniformity read quickly

options.label: all quick
options.consequence: a review costs about a third as much and misses more of what needs judgement

options.label: all careful
options.consequence: nothing is missed for want of care, and a review costs about three times as much

decision: Should the careful readers cost more than the quick ones?
context: A review sends about twenty readers over the documentation. Each can run on the quick model or the careful one, which costs several times as much and is better at judging whether a sentence is true. Today eleven read carefully and eight read quickly, chosen by what each is looking for.

options.label: both
options.consequence: the record keeps everything, and your list gets one line each under a heading the end-of-turn guard does not count, so nothing puts a session to work on it unasked

options.label: the record only
options.consequence: your list stays exactly what you put in it, and unfinished work is visible only when you open the review

decision: When a review runs out of budget, where should the unfinished work go?
context: A review stops when its budget is spent, sometimes with things it found and did not fix. Those can be written into your own list of outstanding work, or left only in the record of that review, which you would have to open to see.
